items.title: Used home prices up €34,250 year-on-year
items.body: Buying an 80-square-meter second-hand home in Spain now costs €253,270 on average, €34,250 more than a year ago. Prices rose 15.6% year-on-year in August, with the average price per square meter at €3,166. The market has now seen 70 consecutive months of price increases. Murcia leads regional rises at 28.8%, and 13 regions have increases above 10%.

items.title: Euribor hits 2.95%, highest in two years
items.body: The Euribor closed August at 2.95%, its highest level since August 2024, up 11 basis points from July and 84 basis points year-on-year. A €150,000 variable-rate mortgage will see monthly payments rise by €70.25, or €843 per year. The data is preliminary, pending confirmation by the Bank of Spain.

items.title: Electricity bills and back-to-school costs squeeze families
items.body: The average regulated electricity bill hit €88.81 in August, up 19% year-on-year and the highest for August since 2022. Back-to-school costs now reach €2,484 per child, 4% more than last year and €514 more than in 2019. Fuel and electricity drove inflation to a three-year high. Madrid and Catalonia remain the most expensive regions.

items.title: Diesel refill costs €22.70 more than last year
items.body: Filling a 50-liter diesel tank now costs €93.05, €22.70 more than a year ago, while petrol costs €86.15, €12.30 more. Diesel prices rose 15.7% in July, triggering an automatic discount of 20 cents per liter from September; petrol gets a 5-cent discount. Prices have now risen for eight consecutive weeks.

items.title: Ceuta migrant capacity doubled, assaults reported
items.body: The government has doubled temporary accommodation places for adult migrants in Ceuta from 1,800 to more than 3,300 in one week and aims for 6,000. Pedro Sánchez ruled out transferring migrants to the mainland. Authorities expelled 200 migrants after detentions for alleged crimes. The Prosecutor's Office recorded 23 sexual assaults in Ceuta in the last month, with eight suspects identified.

items.title: Heat waves leave record 5,200 deaths
items.body: Deaths attributable to high temperatures this summer reached 5,232, the highest since the MoMo monitoring system began in 2015. The previous deadliest summers were 2022 with 4,789 deaths and 2025 with 3,832. August alone recorded 2,147 deaths, a figure likely to exceed the 2,184 from August 2025.

items.title: Spain launches largest wetland restoration in EU history
items.body: Spain will restore 26,100 hectares of wetlands across all 17 autonomous communities over a decade, mobilizing up to €271 million. It is the most ambitious project in the EU LIFE program's history. Ten of the 107 sites are already confirmed. Spanish wetlands are the most diverse in Europe and third most numerous in the world.

items.title: Ceuta gets €168 million ERTE and hiring boost
items.body: The government will approve a €168 million emergency plan for Ceuta, equal to 8% of the territory's GDP. The reinforced ERTE will grant unemployment benefits without prior contributions, and hiring bonuses will rise from 50% to 75%. Companies can receive 100% bonuses. The measures will also apply in Melilla.

items.title: INSS switches disability claims to electronic notifications
items.body: Starting Sept. 1, Social Security will replace paper letters with electronic notifications for all temporary or permanent disability applications. Applicants may receive SMS or email alerts, but legal documents are available via the electronic office. Safeguards remain for people with limited digital access.

items.title: Madrid requires empadronamiento for youth transport pass
items.body: Since June, the Community of Madrid has required applicants to have empadronamiento (municipal registration) to obtain personal transport passes. The change affects thousands of young people, including students arriving for the academic year. A student without registration will see annual transport costs rise from €90 to €500.

items.title: Spain extends Italy border controls 15 days
items.body: Spain has extended border controls for passengers arriving by sea or air from Italy for 15 more days. The move responds to Italy's decision to prolong the suspension of the Schengen agreement with Spain. Travelers between the two countries may face extra checks and delays.

items.title: Airbus Spain workers vote to continue strike
items.body: Workers at Airbus plants in Getafe, San Pablo and Tablada voted to continue their indefinite strike. Employees at Illescas voted last Friday to pause the mobilization. The decisions were made in assemblies this Monday. The impact is limited to specific plants.
